title: Conditional Quantile Adjusted Conformal Prediction for Time Series
topic: General Machine Learning->Sequential, Network, and Time Series Modeling
claim: A prior sequential method yields jagged, non-nested, volatile intervals across confidence levels; ours gives smooth, monotonically nested intervals.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels sharing x-axis; orange jagged vs blue smooth shaded bands
description: Two side-by-side line plots with shaded bands share a y-axis range from about -25 to 3 and an x-axis labeled 'Target Confidence Level', running from 75% to about 99%. The left panel, titled SPCI, is orange. Its upper and lower bounds are jagged and step-like. They fluctuate, jump at around 88% and 92%, and then flatten into constant plateaus past 91%, so the band stops widening. The right panel, titled CQACP, is blue. Its upper and lower bounds are smooth curves that fan out steadily and monotonically, widening sharply near 99%. This gives clean nested intervals. The eye goes first to the contrast between the erratic orange band and the smooth blue funnel. Light gray gridlines and bold axis labels keep the figure minimal.
caption: Comparison of prediction intervals across confidence
abstract: Conformal prediction is challenging for time series with time-varying conditional distributions. Existing sequential conformal methods can yield volatile, non-nested prediction intervals due to noisy tail conditional quantile estimation and quantile crossing issue. To overcome these challenges, we construct prediction intervals for time series via a novel method called Conditional Quantile Adjusted Conformal Prediction (CQACP), which stabilizes sequential conformal calibration by modeling the conditional quantile curve of nonconformity score. At each time step, CQACP evaluates a base conditional quantile learner on a grid of quantile levels and fits a Cornish--Fisher approximation parameterized by conditional moments of nonconformity score with monotonicity constraints. Asymptotically, we prove the conditional validity of the prediction interval under serial dependence and show improved conditional quantile estimation accuracy. Experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that CQACP maintains accurate coverage and produces smooth, narrow, and nested prediction intervals across different significance levels and prediction models.
